referents.why: The him of 'say to him' is the one Moses is sent to, Pharaoh (w13), named in cl2 as the one to stand before and in cl7 as the addressee of the quoted command; masculine singular agrees.
referents.category: pronoun for the addressee of a commanded saying

referents.why: The my of 'my people' is inside the quoted speech introduced by cl6 'thus he says Yahweh', so its speaker is the LORD of that speech (w25); a first person refers to the speaker of the speech it sits in.
referents.category: first person inside a quoted divine speech

referents.why: The me of 'serve me' is in the same quoted speech; its speaker is w25 and the morphology is first common singular.
referents.category: first person inside a quoted divine speech

referents.why: The implied you of the command 'rise early' is the addressee of the outer speech (turn0), Moses (w4); second person masculine singular.
referents.category: implied you of a command in the outer speech

referents.why: The implied you of 'present yourself' is the same command addressee, Moses (w4).
referents.category: implied you of a command in the outer speech

referents.why: The implied you of 'you will say to him' is the one addressed in the outer speech, Moses (w4), who is to carry the message; second person.
referents.category: implied you of a commanded saying

referents.why: The implied you of 'let go' is in the quoted speech that the commanded saying carries, addressed to the one it is said to, Pharaoh (w13); second masculine singular fits.
referents.category: implied you in a quoted command

referents.why: The they of 'that they may serve me' is the people (w27); a collective noun taking a plural verb, and serving fits the people.

links.why: cl3 is the presentative there inside the speech to Moses that cl0 introduces; a wayyiqtol continues the narrative line from a clause outside the speech, not from one inside it.
links.category: narrative link taken from inside a speech

links.why: Two second-person commands joined by plain waw; no cause, result or purpose is required.
The weqatal cl5 continues what precedes it; cl4 is the participle that sets the time of the saying, so the sequence holds.
The waw joins a second-person command to a third-person yiqtol, a change of person, which the and type gives as so that rather than plain and.
links.category: waw joins a command to a change of person

links.why: The third-person yiqtol after the command states what the command is for: that they may serve me.
cl6 is the frame of the quoted speech; what is said is the command with its purpose, the whole imperative group, not only its first command.
links.category: speech frame and what is said

groups.why: The outer speech, the LORD to Moses. Its parts are the command group, the presentative and the participle clause of time, and the commanded turn g1; the old list put cl1 to cl5 in directly and left out the nesting.
groups.category: outer speech with a commanded speech nested in it

groups.why: Two commands joined by plain waw at one level are one imperative group with two command members; part is not a member role of this kind, and these commands bring about no effect.
groups.category: commands joined by and at one level

groups.why: The commanded turn: Moses is told to say to Pharaoh. Its frame is the saying clause cl5, sender Moses, addressee Pharaoh, and what is said is the quoted turn1.
groups.category: speech commanded to a third party

groups.why: The quoted speech: frame cl6, sender the LORD (w25). Its addressee, Pharaoh, is not named in the clause and is inherited from g1. Its part is the command group, not two loose clauses.
One command with what it brings about: cl8 is the third-person yiqtol after the waw, so it is the group's effect as well as the purpose link from cl7.
groups.category: command with its purpose as effect

none_fit.where: cl0 (wayyiqtol he said), before the verse
none_fit.what: Narrative continuation from Exo.8.15#cl3, the last narrative clause of the previous verse. The then type is within-verse only, and the episode rung it defers to is not in link_types, so the link is not written.
A presentative behold with a participle giving the time of the saying (when Pharaoh goes out). No link type expresses a temporal when-clause; when_if_though covers only a fronted ki.

cant_tell.what: The scope of the time clause cl3 and cl4: does it set the time for the standing before Pharaoh (cl2), or only for the saying (cl5)?
cant_tell.why: The text has one presentative and no connective, so the form does not settle which command it governs. The then link from cl4 to cl5 is kept on the reading that the saying follows the going out.
